cards.explanation: The answer is whether it can save him. James asks, "Can such faith save him?" He's talking about someone who claims to have faith but has no deeds (James 2:14). Then he leaves the question hanging in the air, and I think he wants his readers to feel it.

The answer is clothes and daily food. James says this brother or sister is "…without clothes and daily food." (James 2:15) Those are the basics, the stuff you need every single day. Notice he calls them a brother or sister, friends, so this is a fellow believer, someone close.

The word is dead. James says faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is dead (James 2:17). He's not saying that faith is small or sleepy. He chose a strong word on purpose, and he lets it sit there.

James answers that he'll show his faith by his deeds. He says, "Show me your faith without deeds, and I will show you my faith by my deeds." (James 2:18) He doesn't argue about it. He says you can see it. I think he's saying real faith has something you can point to.

The answer is False. James says even the demons believe that God is one, and they shudder (James 2:19). That's the opposite of rejoicing. I shudder when I find a burnt batch at the bottom of the oven, friends, and I'm guessing it isn't the same thing, but the word is the word.

The answer is working with them. James writes that Abraham's "…faith was working with his actions…" (James 2:22) His faith and his actions were working together, like my stamp and my mustache on the same cookie. James puts them side by side.

The word is perfected. James says Abraham's faith was perfected by what he did (James 2:22). I think of a stamp pressed all the way down, where the shape finally shows clearly. That's my picture, bakers, and James's word is perfected.

The answer is False. James says, "…a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone." (James 2:24) He just walked through Abraham's story, and that's where he ended up. So faith never stands alone in his picture.

The answer is that she welcomed the spies and sent them off another way. James says Rahab welcomed the spies and sent them off on another route (James 2:25). That's the action he points to. Joshua 2:4 adds that she took the two men and hid them, and that's part of her story too.

The answer is a body without the spirit. James says, "As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without deeds is dead." (James 2:26) A body with no spirit is lifeless, and he says faith without deeds is the same. It's a plain picture for a plain point, friends.
